claim: meta-tegra wrynose README targets Jetson Linux R39.2.1 / JetPack 7.2.1 and lists Jetson AGX Thor devkit, AGX Orin devkit, Orin NX 16GB (p3509 and p3768 carriers), Orin Nano devkit and AGX Orin Industrial 64GB (P3701-0008); machine confs include jetson-agx-thor-t4000

meta-tegra wrynose carries recipes-kernel/linux/linux-yocto_6.18.bbappend and linux-yocto-rt_6.18.bbappend; linux-yocto-tegra.inc sets COMPATIBLE_MACHINE:tegra = (tegra234|tegra264) and pulls OE4T tegra-kernel-cache branch yocto-6.18 as kmeta; the branch head commit (2026-11-11) is 'linux-yocto: bump SRCREV_tegrameta for 6.18.54'

meta-tegra's default kernel remains NVIDIA's: tegra-common.inc sets PREFERRED_PROVIDER_virtual/kernel ?= linux-noble-nvidia-tegra (6.8) and derives TEGRA_USING_VENDOR_KERNEL from it; linux-yocto 6.18 is an opt-in alternative

The linux-yocto Jetson path is new: commit e508ec6 'linux-yocto_6.18: add tegra264 support via tegra-kernel-cache kmeta' and d1878bb 'add RT bbappend' landed 2026-07-26; 2e25c41 'factor out check for vendor kernel' 2026-08-30

nvidia-kernel-oot.inc (COMPATIBLE_MACHINE tegra) builds NVIDIA's out-of-tree modules (host1x, nvmap, nvgpu compute package for tegra234) and has a linux-yocto-specific make-flag set that only skips the Realtek RTL8822CE/RTL8852CE Wi-Fi modules when linux-yocto is the kernel provider [status note: recipe read; runtime not tested]

OE4T tegra-kernel-cache yocto-6.18 (created 2026-07-20) holds 463 patches: 217 'platform' (from NVIDIA linux/patches/<ver>), 240 'sauce' (NVIDIA integration branch, reference-filtered), 5 distro, 1 rt-compat; it has tegra234 and tegra264 standard and preempt-rt BSP descriptions; contributors kekiefer (19 commits) and ichergui (4)

OE4T/meta-tegra is MIT-licensed with 585 stars; top contributors by commits: madisongh 2375, ichergui 189, kekiefer 169, dwalkes 53 [LEDGER 2026-11-11: re-pinned: LICENSE at this SHA is MIT; stars and contributor counts are API metadata at access]
Yocto Project releases page: Wrynose (6.0, April 2026) is Long Term Support until April 2030; Scarthgap (5.0) LTS until April 2028; 'Future LTS releases are planned for 4 years'

OE4T 'Which branch' page: wrynose (LTS) and blacksail (non-LTS) track L4T R39.2.1/JetPack 7.2.1 for AGX Orin/Orin NX/Orin Nano/AGX Thor; scarthgap (LTS) tracks R36.5.2/JetPack 6.2.3 'will stay on R36.x/JetPack 6.x'; no stated support duration

balenaOS for Jetson Orin (balena-os/balena-jetson-orin master) builds on the OE4T meta-tegra wrynose branch (git submodule layers/meta-tegra, branch = wrynose) plus a CompuLab meta-tegra-compulab layer
NVIDIA Jetson product lifecycle: Jetson T5000 available to August 2035, T4000 to January 2036; AGX Orin 64/32GB, Orin NX 16/8GB, Orin Nano 8/4GB to January 2032; AGX Orin Industrial to July 2033

NVIDIA (2026-10-30): 'JetPack 5.1.8 marks the final release for JetPack 5 series' and users 'will no longer receive any critical updates'; NVIDIA points to ecosystem partner RidgeRun for continued JetPack 5 kernel support

NVIDIA JetPack page: 'With JetPack 7, Jetson software aligns with the Server Base System Architecture (SBSA)'; 'Jetson Thor is based on the SBSA stack'; 'NVIDIA now officially supports Yocto Project' with 'Full-stack, NVIDIA-validated recipes and reference images ... through OE4T'; no lifecycle stated

Jetson Linux r39.2 nv-load-display-modules: Orin uses nvgpu.ko for graphics/compute; Thor has 'a combined graphics, compute, and display driver in nvidia.ko' (OpenRM, updates/opensource-gpu-disp); 'a single root file system can be used across both Jetson Orin and Jetson Thor devices'

CUDA 13.5 Linux install guide: Debian 13 is listed for amd64 and arm64 (SBSA) but not for Jetson; the only 'arm64 sbsa Jetson' rows are 'Ubuntu 24.04 LTS Rel39 (JP7.2) native' and 'cross'; native Jetson repos are arm64-sbsa-jetson-openrm (Thor, + cuda-compat) and arm64-sbsa-jetson-nvgpu (Orin, + cuda-compat-orin); cross development for arm64-sbsa-jetson only on Ubuntu 24.04 [status note: narrows C-W18-027]

NVIDIA r39.2.1 Bring Your Own Kernel: 'NVIDIA has provided a set of out-of-tree modules for drivers that cannot be upstreamed or that have not yet been upstreamed'; the NVIDIA kernel 'is considered to be the most complete and best tested source code for Tegra devices'; patch list runs from v5.15 to next; no list of features lost

siderolabs/pkgs PR #1518 (nvgpu for Orin on the Talos mainline kernel) is open, approved 2026-11-02; CUDA verified on Orin NX 16GB on 6.18.24 and 6.18.48 (about 64-78 tok/s on qwen2.5:0.5b) and AGX Orin 64GB; on 7.3.0 throughput fell to about 10 tok/s (suspected SMCCC change, unresolved 2026-11-04); GA10B firmware not in linux-firmware

yeetypete/bootc-jetson (MIT, 6 stars, created 2026-06-07) is a 'reference example' bootc image for Orin and Thor on JetPack 7.2: Ubuntu 24.04 + L4T packages, a custom nvidia-l4t-kernel 6.8 build with EROFS and FS_VERITY, composefs backend, sealed UKI booted by systemd-boot; not intended to be consumed in production

meta-tegra NVIDIA-Container-Runtime doc: NVIDIA's Jetson containers 'do not bundle most hardware-specific libraries, but expect them to be provided by the host OS'; TensorRT, cuDNN and other JetPack components must be included in the image

meta-tegra redundant-rootfs doc: NVIDIA's bootloader/rootfs A/B pairing plus UEFI capsule update can be driven by 'swupdate, rauc, mender, or others'; both stock JetPack and OE4T images default to non-redundant layouts (USE_REDUNDANT_FLASH_LAYOUT_DEFAULT = 1 to change)
rauc/meta-rauc-community master has layers for genericx86-64, raspberrypi, rockchip, nxp, sunxi, beaglebone and qemu, but no Tegra layer

meta-tegra added Jetson Linux CVE metadata to its NVIDIA recipes on 2026-09-19 (commits 839e0be 'nvidia-kernel-oot: add Jetson Linux CVE metadata' and dc689c1 'tegra-binaries: add Jetson Linux CVE metadata'), feeding Yocto's CVE/SBOM tooling
